topic: 5 things you need to know: one hacker used AI agents to break into 100+ company websites
post:
One hacker. A short prompt. AI agents that broke into 100+ company websites. 🔓
Here are 5 things you need to know.

1️⃣ What happened
Reuters reports that a Chinese-speaking hacker used AI agents to break into websites of more than 100 companies, including Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins.

2️⃣ The instructions were tiny
The hacker's instructions were under 100 Chinese characters. Then the agents worked for hours with little direction.

3️⃣ It hit a big list
The agents tried more than 1,200 sites, mostly online stores in the US, Canada, Australia and Japan.

4️⃣ It was cheap
The researcher who found it estimated about $5,000 in AI costs, though he said that number is highly uncertain.

5️⃣ It was found by accident
A researcher spotted it through the attacker's own exposed control panels for an open-source agent tool. Reuters couldn't tell how much data, if any, was taken.

Why it matters:
AI agents don't just help defenders. They let one person do the work of a whole team, on either side. 🛡️

Practical takeaway:
Ask your team this week: which of our websites are run by third parties, and when were they last patched? 🔍

Is your company ready for attacks run by AI agents? 👇
